lesson-intro.text: A canoe goes wherever its paddle takes it. Ours has the paddle resting across it, in front. Watch which lines stop at the paddle, then push off with your pen.

top.text: A canoe is shaped like a long smile. Draw the top edge from tip to tip, dipping in the middle.

shaft.text: The paddle leans across the canoe. Draw its small handle, then a straight shaft down past the edge.

blade.text: The blade is a long, rounded leaf on the end of the shaft.

bottom-left.text: Now the canoe's belly. From the left tip, curve down and along until you bump into the blade.

bottom-right.text: Carry on past the blade, and rise to the right tip.

trim.text: Two trim lines follow the top edge, one on each side of the paddle.

paddle-brown.text: Color the blade and the handle brown.

lesson-outro.text: Canoe and paddle, waiting at the water's edge. Where would you paddle to?
